title: General electronics fault
shortDescription: The main control has reported a generic internal fault.
fullDescription:
F0 on a Miele refrigerator is a catch-all code. The control has detected a condition that does not map to a more specific F code, usually after a surge or brownout.

A hard power reset clears many F0 events. Persistent F0 needs service.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes and plug back in.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Book a Miele technician if the code returns within a day.

whenToCallPro: Call Miele service if F0 returns after a reset.

faq.a: Usually yes during the brief reset window.

title: Fridge sensor fault
shortDescription: The fresh-food compartment temperature sensor is out of range.
fullDescription:
F1 means the NTC sensor in the refrigerator compartment is open or shorted. Miele uses it to drive the air damper and compressor request, so regulation fails without it.

Food may over-cool or warm depending on the sensor's failure mode.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the light cover and swap the NTC sensor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor is hidden behind the liner and you cannot reach it.

faq.a: Yes, temperature control is disabled in one compartment.

title: Freezer sensor fault
shortDescription: The freezer compartment sensor reads out of range.
fullDescription:
F2 indicates the freezer NTC sensor is open or shorted. The compressor logic falls back to a safe default, but the freezer may run too cold or too warm.

Replace the sensor to restore regulation.
symptoms: Freezer too warm or rock hard

fixSteps.title: Defrost manually
fixSteps.instruction: Empty the freezer and let it defrost 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Replace NTC
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the freezer evaporator cover and swap the sensor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if ice damage reaches the wiring inside the liner.

faq.a: Only if it stayed below 5C during the fault.

title: Evaporator sensor fault
shortDescription: The evaporator coil sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription:
F3 means the defrost termination sensor on the freezer evaporator is not reading correctly. The unit may skip or over-extend defrost cycles, leading to frost buildup.

The fix is a sensor replacement behind the evaporator cover.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the evaporator cover and swap the coil NTC.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the evaporator cover is held by hidden clips you cannot release.

faq.a: Without defrost, frost collects until airflow collapses.

title: Defrost heater fault
shortDescription: The defrost heater did not raise the evaporator temperature.
fullDescription:
F4 indicates a failed defrost cycle: the heater did not warm the evaporator enough in the allotted time. Either the heater element is open, the thermal fuse blew, or the wiring is broken.

Without defrost, the freezer will eventually stop cooling as ice plugs the airflow.

fixSteps.title: Manual defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty the freezer and defrost for 24 hours.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Check the heater and fuse for continuity; replace the failed component.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the evaporator is iced solid and requires steaming.

faq.a: A few days at most; otherwise freezer fails.

title: Air damper motor fault
shortDescription: The motorized air damper between compartments is not responding.
fullDescription:
F10 means the damper that distributes cold air between the freezer and fridge is not moving or its feedback is missing. Either the motor is stalled or the limit switches have failed.

The compartments will drift out of regulation; usually the fridge gets too warm.
symptoms: Fridge too warm but freezer normal

fixSteps.title: Defrost
fixSteps.instruction: Empty and let the unit defrost overnight to free any frozen flap.

fixSteps.title: Replace damper
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new damper assembly if the fault persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the damper lives behind the liner of an integrated unit.

faq.q: Why only the fridge gets warm?
faq.a: The damper starves the fridge of cold air while the freezer coil runs.

title: Compressor start failure
shortDescription: The compressor did not start after multiple attempts.
fullDescription:
F50 means the control tried to start the compressor several times and did not see the expected current. Common causes are a seized compressor, a bad start relay, or a failed inverter.

Cooling stops until repair.

fixSteps.title: Power reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 30 minutes and retry once.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Technician will diagnose the compressor and relay.

whenToCallPro: Always call Miele service; sealed system work is regulated.

faq.a: Move to another unit; cooling will not resume quickly.

title: Compressor overcurrent
shortDescription: The compressor drew more current than allowed.
fullDescription:
F52 trips when the compressor motor draws abnormal current for more than a few seconds, usually because it is starting against high pressure or partially seized.

Often recoverable after a long off-cycle; persistent F52 is a failing compressor.

fixSteps.title: Long rest
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60 minutes to equalize system pressures.

fixSteps.title: Retry once
fixSteps.instruction: Plug back in and observe; if F52 returns, call service.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if F52 returns after a 60-minute rest.

title: Door switch fault
shortDescription: The door reed switch is not reporting correctly.
fullDescription:
F71 appears when the control cannot read a plausible door state. The interior light may not switch off, or the temperature alarm may lag.

A cracked door switch, a broken magnet, or a bent hinge are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Check alignment
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure the door closes flush and the hinge is not sagging.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the reed switch in the cabinet frame.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the hinge itself is bent on an integrated unit.
videoSearchQuery: Miele refrigerator F71 door switch fix

faq.q: Can I still use the fridge?
faq.a: Yes, but cooling may be less efficient with the light on.

title: Ice maker fault
shortDescription: The ice maker is not completing a cycle.
fullDescription:
F84 indicates the ice maker module reported a stuck cycle, usually because the mold did not empty or the fill tube froze.

Disable the ice maker, thaw the tube, and restart.

fixSteps.title: Turn off ice maker
fixSteps.instruction: Use the interface to disable ice.

fixSteps.title: Thaw fill tube
fixSteps.instruction: Use a hair dryer on low heat to thaw the fill tube at the back of the compartment.

fixSteps.title: Replace module
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists, install a new ice maker module.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the water line under the unit is leaking.

title: Water inlet valve fault
shortDescription: The ice maker water valve did not open or closed when commanded.
fullDescription:
F85 means the solenoid on the water inlet valve is not responding. Either the valve coil is open, the water is shut off at the supply, or the screen filter is clogged.

No water flows to the ice maker until repaired.

fixSteps.title: Check water supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the shutoff behind the fridge is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet screen
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the water line and rinse the inlet screen.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the inlet valve if cleaning does not restore flow.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the water line has compression fittings you have not worked with.

faq.a: Yes, that clears the alarm for now.

title: Communication bus fault
shortDescription: Internal MieleBus communication between modules failed.
fullDescription:
F220 means nodes on the internal communication bus are not responding. On integrated Miele refrigerators, several modules share a serial bus, and any broken connector or bad module can pull it down.

Cooling may still happen in fallback mode, but user controls will be limited.

fixSteps.title: Reseat connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Technician should check each bus connector in turn.

whenToCallPro: Always call Miele service; bus diagnostics need the dealer tool.
